story.title: USS George Washington Deploys to Middle East Amid Concerns Over USS Lincoln's Conditions
story.summary: The USS George Washington aircraft carrier is en route to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has faced reports of declining mental health and supply issues among its crew during its record 260-day deployment. Some sailors aboard the Lincoln have reportedly attempted self-harm due to the conditions. However, U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has disputed these reports, calling them misrepresented, and senators are calling for an investigation into the situation.

related_stories.title: US Missionary Kevin Rideout Released After Kidnapping in Niger
related_stories.summary: Kevin Rideout, an American missionary kidnapped in Niger last October, has been released after nine months in captivity. He is reported to be in good health and is currently in the care of US officials. His organization, SIM International, stated that he would soon be reunited with his family.

related_stories.title: Ebola Outbreak in DRC Expands to Sixth Province Amid Rising Death Toll
related_stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has now spread to a sixth province, Bas-Uele, following the death of a man who traveled from Haut-Uele. The World Health Organization has indicated that this outbreak is on track to become the deadliest in history, surpassing the previous record of over 11,000 fatalities from a decade ago. Currently, more than 2,100 deaths have been reported out of over 4,500 cases.

related_stories.title: Zambians Vote in Presidential Election Amid Economic Concerns
related_stories.summary: Zambians voted on Thursday in a presidential election that tests the economic reforms of incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema. Approximately 8 million registered voters also selected members of Parliament and local councilors. Vote counting is currently underway, with results expected on Monday.
